## How it works

<h3>Try it</h3><ol><li>Compare the building with the surrounding buildings and street map.</li><li>Open Files (folder) on the left toolbar and toggle the checkbox beside OMG_KS_3dBAG.ifc to distinguish project geometry from its neighbours.</li><li>Zoom to the project boundary to inspect its relationship to the nearby buildings.</li></ol><h2>Developer integration</h2>
<p>Use <code>const api = await viewer.IfcAPI</code> to obtain the complete native web-ifc instance supplied by the SDK. Call <code>Init()</code> and <code>OpenModel()</code> for each downloaded IFC. This API runs on the main thread and owns its models independently of the viewer.</p>
<p>This example reads the project, site and geometric contexts through web-ifc. It updates the site coordinates and true north, writes the IFC2X3 <code>ePSet_ProjectedCRS</code> and <code>ePSet_MapConversion</code> property sets with <code>CreateIfcEntity()</code>, <code>CreateIfcType()</code> and <code>WriteLine()</code>, then saves the edited bytes with <code>SaveModel()</code>.</p>
<p>The native model is closed and WASM disposed before the saved bytes are passed to <code>viewer.add()</code>. After all three files load, <code>viewer.toggleMap(true)</code> displays their corrected placement. Native vectors are released explicitly. Repeated access to <code>viewer.IfcAPI</code> returns the same instance, which is initialized again for the next file. Geometry and local heights are retained, and the original downloads are not overwritten.</p>
<p>See the <a href="https://thatopen.github.io/engine_web-ifc/docs/classes/web-ifc.IfcAPI.html">complete web-ifc API reference</a> for all native methods.</p><p>Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP, for example <code>python -m http.server 8080</code>. Open <code>http://localhost:8080/</code>; the SDK and sample downloads require internet access.</p>
<h3>Model notes</h3><p>Georeferencing corrected; geometry retained. Heights are local.</p>

<p>The example corrects IFC georeferencing metadata using the published S1 horizontal placement before normal import. Original geometry is retained. Local model heights are used; no surveyed elevation is claimed.</p>
